entry.title: AI Layer Separation in Photoshop: Pulling a Flat Design Apart
entry.summary: What layer separation delivers today. A tested walkthrough that rebuilds a flat poster as editable Photoshop layers, element by element, with every limit named.
entry.content:
A flattened design is a dead end. The export looks finished, the working file is gone or was never yours, and the next request is always the same: move the headline, swap the product, extend the background for a different crop.

Layer separation is the idea that a model can hand those parts back to you, and the capability is real. ByteDance documents it for Seedream 5.0 Pro: one request returns a base image plus up to 16 transparent layers, each tagged with its stacking order and position. Whether you can reach it depends entirely on how you call the model. In our own testing on October 15, 2026, the Astria endpoints returned a single flat image rather than layers, so this article covers the route that does work today: extracting one element per request and assembling the returns yourself.

That route is slower than the promise. It is also good enough to rebuild a poster as an editable document, which is what we did below, failures included.

What the model can do natively​

Worth knowing before you judge any workflow against it. ByteDance's image generation API exposes a layer_decomposition flag on Seedream 5.0 Pro and 5.0 Flash. When set, the documented behaviour is:

  • one base image plus up to 16 layers, each returned as a PNG with a real alpha channel
  • placement metadata per layer: a stacking index and a bounding box in both pixel and normalised coordinates, so a caller can reassemble the stack
  • a single input image only, at 1K, 1.5K or 2K, with no 4K path in this mode
  • an optional prompt that targets specific elements, or no prompt at all to let the model pick them
  • no partial success: if one layer fails, the whole request fails

ByteDance's launch material also describes the background behind a removed subject being reconstructed. That claim appears in its product blog rather than the API specification, so treat it as the vendor's description.

Two things follow. The output is separate PNGs plus coordinates, not a PSD — reassembly is the caller's job either way. And layered mode is capped at 2K, so a layer-separation asset is never a 4K hero.

What we tested, and what came back​

Every image below comes from one supplied photograph of a skincare tube at 4000 by 6000 pixels. Nothing here is text-to-image.

First we built something worth pulling apart. Seedream 5 Pro composed a finished campaign poster from that product reference: product on a stone pedestal, foliage behind it, a lilac gradient, a headline and a subtitle. That composite became the input for every separation attempt that followed.

Then six requests against that composite.

RequestModelWhat came backTransparency
The documented layer flag, set explicitlySeedream 5 ProOne flat image. The flag had no effect on the responseNone
Split into independent transparent layers, in wordsSeedream 5 ProOne flat image, the poster re-rendered largely unchangedNone
Isolate the product onlySeedream 5 ProProduct cleanly isolated on a flat white field, label intactNone
Reconstruct the background with every element removedSeedream 5 ProClean plate, gradient and floor rebuilt, no trace of the objectsNone
Isolate the headline and subtitle typeSeedream 5 ProLettering on a flat white field, typeface and spacing preservedNone
Return a PNG with a real alpha channelGPT Image 2.5 SunburstA PNG container with no alpha channel, RGB onlyNone

The first row is the one that matters. The documented capability is not reachable through the endpoints we tested, and nothing we ran returned an alpha channel, including the model whose provider documents transparency support. The PNG arrived as a PNG and carried no transparency once inspected.

What the extractions actually look like​

The per-element results are the reason to carry on.

The typography result is the surprise. Asked for the lettering alone, the model reproduced the same geometric sans at the same weight and letter spacing rather than paraphrasing it into a lookalike. That is the difference between a layer you can reposition and a layer you have to rebuild.

The clean plate is the quiet workhorse. Once the background exists as its own image with nothing standing on it, every other element is free to move.

The working sequence​

Four passes, in this order, each one request against the same flattened source.

Pass one, the clean plate. Remove everything and rebuild what was behind it. Name the objects you want gone, and say explicitly that the surface and gradient must be reconstructed where they stood. Do this first: it is the layer everything else sits on, and if the model cannot rebuild the background convincingly, the rest of the exercise is not worth running.

Pass two, the hero element. Isolate the product, the subject, the single thing the layout is about. Ask for a flat, even field behind it rather than transparency, because that is what you will reliably get and it masks cleanly.

Pass three, the type. Request the lettering alone, and name what must survive: the exact typeface, weight, spacing and position. Vague requests here produce a plausible headline in the wrong font, which is worse than no layer at all.

Pass four, the props. Foliage, pedestal, secondary objects, one request each. Resist the urge to batch them. Every element you add to a single request raises the chance the model reinterprets the whole frame instead of extracting a part of it.

Then assemble: clean plate at the bottom, props, hero, type on top, masking the flat field behind each extraction. What you have at the end is the thing the flat export denied you, a layout where the headline can move, the product can be replaced and the canvas can extend for a different aspect ratio.

Working inside the Astria Photoshop plugin, each pass returns into the open document as its own layer, which removes the four browser round trips and the registration drift that comes with them. The plugin guide covers the panel itself.

The limits, stated plainly​

Be honest with yourself about what this is before you promise it to a client.

It is not one click. Four or five requests per design, plus masking. For a single hero layout that is a good trade. For two hundred SKUs it is a staffing problem, and that work belongs in a production pipeline instead.

It is reconstruction, not recovery. The model is not reading hidden layer data out of a flattened file, because there is none. It generates a plausible version of each part. The product that comes back is a very good likeness, not the original pixels. For a visual, a mockup or a layout study that is fine. For a regulated label, a legal mark or print artwork it is not. Keep the approved artwork.

Expect flat fields, not cutouts. Nothing we tested returned a transparent layer or a layered file, so plan to mask.

Fine detail degrades. Isolated elements come back at the model's own resolution and interpretation. Check small type, edge quality and any geometry a customer would recognise before the layer reaches a deliverable.

One element per pass. Both all-at-once attempts failed in our test, and we would not plan around that changing.

Where the field stands​

Useful context, because this capability is moving quickly and the marketing runs ahead of the shipping.

Photoshop does not do this yet. Adobe announced Layered Image Editing, described as automatically separating objects in an image onto different layers, at MAX in October 2025, and still labels it in development. No current Photoshop or Firefly feature list documents the capability. Generative Fill is a different tool: it writes a generated result for the selection you made, rather than taking a finished composition apart.

Affinity shipped it first among the big editors. Canva announced AI-assisted Scene Decomposition for Affinity in September 2026, described as splitting a flattened image back into editable layers, unlocked with a Canva premium plan.

Seedream is not the only model that can do it. Alibaba's Qwen-Image-Layered, released as open weights in December 2025, decomposes an image into RGBA layers with the layer count set by the prompt.

Plugins are ahead of hosts. Higgsfield's Photoshop plugin has carried a Layer Decompose tool since June 2026, offering 1K to 2K output and an adjustable layer count. Its own pages describe its web Layers editor as powered by Seedream 5.0, while the plugin documentation names no engine.

The direction is clear even if the dates are not. Treat any single result, including ours, as a snapshot.

Where it earns its place​

  • The working file is gone. An agency folded, a freelancer moved on, or all that survives is a JPEG from a sign-off email.
  • One layout, many crops. A campaign image has to become a 4:5, a story, a banner and a PDP tile. With the background as its own layer, the recrop is composition rather than a new shoot.
  • Market and seasonal variants. The typography changes per language or promotion while the photography stays.
  • Posters, layouts and design studies. Dense work with several discrete elements is exactly where pulling parts out beats painting them out. Our packaging mockup guide covers the generation side of related work.

Prompt patterns that worked​

Short and specific beat long and descriptive in every pass we ran.

  • Name the elements to remove individually rather than saying "remove everything".
  • Say what must be reconstructed, not only what must go: "rebuilding the surface and gradient where the objects used to be".
  • For type, list the attributes to preserve: typeface, weight, spacing, position.
  • Ask for a flat, even background behind an isolated element instead of requesting transparency.
  • Keep one element per request.

Frequently asked questions​

What is AI layer separation?​

Taking a finished, flattened design and recovering its parts as separate editable pieces: the subject, the typography, the props and the background behind them. The goal is a document you can restyle, recrop and re-version without rebuilding the artwork from scratch.

Which models can decompose an image into layers?​

ByteDance documents layer decomposition for Seedream 5.0 Pro and 5.0 Flash, producing one base image plus up to 16 transparent PNG layers with placement metadata, at up to 2K. Alibaba's open-weights Qwen-Image-Layered also decomposes images into RGBA layers. Google's Gemini image models and OpenAI's GPT Image do not document layered output.

Can I get layered output through any image API?​

Only where the integration passes the parameter through. In our October 15, 2026 test the Astria endpoints did not return layered output, with or without the documented flag, so the practical route today is extracting one element per request and assembling those returns as layers in Photoshop.

Does Photoshop separate a flat image into layers?​

Not yet. Adobe announced Layered Image Editing, automatic separation of objects onto layers, at MAX in October 2025 and still lists it as in development. No current Photoshop or Firefly feature list documents the capability. Affinity shipped an AI-assisted Scene Decomposition feature in September 2026, behind a Canva premium plan.

What is layer separation actually useful for?​

Recovering editability you have lost: a flattened export with no working file, a campaign layout that must be recropped for another channel, a design whose typography changes per market, or a subject that has to move to a new background.

Sources and methodology​

All generations ran through Astria on October 15, 2026, in the Articles workspace, from one supplied product photograph at 4000 by 6000 pixels. The composite was built with Seedream 5 Pro at 2K. Five separation attempts ran against that composite with Seedream 5 Pro, including one that set the documented layer flag directly on the request, and one transparency attempt with GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst. Returned files were inspected for dimensions, colour mode and alpha channel before any claim here was written. Prompt identifiers and the full run record are kept in our internal benchmark notes.

This is one design, run once per request. It shows what the endpoints we called do with a dense, text-bearing layout. It is not a success-rate measurement, and a different composition may behave differently.

Capability descriptions for layer decomposition come from ByteDance's image generation API documentation and its Seedream 5.0 Pro launch post. Adobe's Layered Image Editing announcement is from its October 2025 MAX coverage, with the absence of a shipping feature checked against Adobe's current Photoshop and Firefly feature lists. The Affinity capability is from Canva's September 2026 announcement. Qwen-Image-Layered is Alibaba's December 2025 open-weights release. Higgsfield details come from its own plugin and changelog pages. A provider documenting a capability describes that provider's own surface and does not guarantee identical behaviour through every integration, which is exactly what our first test row shows. Model behaviour and output formats change; re-test before building a process on any single result.

entry.title: Fashion Campaign Variations in Photoshop With AI
entry.summary: Explore fashion settings, lighting, framing and poses in Photoshop with the Astria plugin. Prepare clear campaign options for creative and marketing teams.
entry.content:
A creative director wants to compare a rooftop with a beach. A campaign designer needs a full-body composition as well as a closer portrait. A marketing team wants alternatives that change one creative decision at a time.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin lets the team explore those directions from an existing image and keep the options in the same document. Organize the work around setting, styling, lighting and composition so every option answers a clear question.

Watch a fashion concept change setting and framing​

The fashion workflow demonstration revises trousers, reveals more of the model through wider framing, adds and removes sunglasses, changes the setting and time of day, and explores a running pose. The panel contains several model choices; use the model and controls available in your installed version for your own brief.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Separate the creative variables​

The video moves quickly through several transformations. For an approval round, slow the process down and establish which variable each option changes. Keep one approved styling source, then generate a rooftop, beach or studio direction from that source rather than allowing each setting to inherit all the previous changes.

Compare day and evening versions separately from location choices. If one image gains a new pose, sunglasses and a different hair color at the same time, the creative director cannot easily tell which change made it preferable.

Use references for the garment and person when their continuity matters. The visible jacket, closures, stripes and face should remain reviewable across the set. A strong campaign atmosphere does not resolve a changed product detail.

Build compositions around the placement​

A wide image can establish the setting and leave space for a headline. A full-body image makes styling legible. A close portrait emphasizes expression or an accessory. Start with the placement's actual aspect ratio and the part of the product that needs to remain visible.

When extending the frame, inspect everything the model introduces outside the source: feet, trouser hems, ground contact and the direction of shadows. Keep exact headline copy and brand artwork on ordinary Photoshop layers after the image direction has been selected.

Give creative and marketing teams different review criteria​

RoleApplicationReview question
Creative directorCompare campaign worlds and visual moodDoes the direction express the brief?
Fashion designer or stylistCheck wardrobe and accessoriesDoes the actual product remain recognizable?
Campaign production artistRefine composition and masksWill the image work at the required crop and size?
Performance marketing designerPrepare controlled creative alternativesWhich attribute differs between the candidates?
Social content leadAdapt an approved direction to placementsIs the product clear in each format?
Creative operations managerOrganize versions and approvalsWhich source and references produced the approved option?

Prepare assets for a useful creative test​

The plugin creates candidate images. Run audience or campaign testing in the team's normal testing system, with the chosen imagery, copy, placement and audience recorded. Keep versions comparable if the question is whether a setting or composition changes performance.

Do not describe a generated alternative as a winning ad before it has been tested. First approve visual quality and product fidelity, then export the selected candidates with a naming convention that identifies the creative difference.

entry.title: Replace Clothing in Photoshop With Product References
entry.summary: Use the Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin to explore garment, shoe and jewelry changes with reference images and a practical fashion approval workflow.
entry.content:
A stylist wants to see a different sweater on the same model. A retoucher needs to replace a shoe without rebuilding the whole photograph. A merchandising team wants to review how accessories work together before approving a look.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin brings the source photograph, product references and generated edits into one document. The useful unit of work is a selected garment or accessory, with the rest of the photograph available for comparison.

Watch the reference editing workflow​

The demonstration uses a seated model and separate references for shoes, a striped sweater and pearl earrings. It also shows why a sweater swap and a jacket removal are different edits: the jacket can continue covering the intended garment unless the brief addresses both.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Choose the reference for the item being changed​

A useful product reference shows the item clearly enough to judge the result. For a sweater, include the neckline, cuffs, hem and repeating pattern. For footwear, show the toe, heel, fastening and profile. For earrings, include the complete shape and enough detail to understand the material.

Prepare one reference per editing decision. A mood board can guide styling, but a clear product photograph is the stronger input when the garment or accessory itself must remain recognizable. Keep the source photograph on an untouched layer and attach the reference from an image file or the relevant Photoshop layer using the current panel.

Replace a garment in a controlled sequence​

  1. Select the region occupied by the item, including the boundary where the new material must meet skin or surrounding clothing.
  2. Attach the product reference and identify which item it should replace. Specify whether an overlapping jacket or accessory should remain.
  3. Describe the intended change and the person, pose, background and framing to preserve.
  4. Generate an alternative and toggle the returned layer against the source.
  5. Refine the mask at cuffs, fingers, hair and garment edges. Use Photoshop adjustments for a local color balance correction.

If the first result already establishes a good sweater, make the next accessory edit from a separately saved version. Keep an approved styling layer available rather than repeatedly changing the only copy. This gives the creative director an intelligible set of options and lets the retoucher undo one decision without rebuilding the rest.

Give each team role a useful deliverable​

RoleApplicationDeliverable
RetoucherLocal garment and accessory replacementLayered PSD with editable masks
StylistCompare shoes, knitwear and jewelry combinationsLabeled styling alternatives
Creative directorEvaluate the approved outfit in the source compositionReview board with the source and selected option
Merchandising teamExplore coordinated collection looksConcepts associated with the actual product references
Ecommerce leadDecide whether a candidate can represent a SKUProduct fidelity review before export

Check the product before approving the photograph​

Read the garment as a product: count stripes, check where the neckline meets the shoulders, inspect the cuffs and hem, and compare fabric appearance with the reference. A plausible sweater is insufficient if the intended item has a different pattern or construction.

Check the surrounding person too. Hands can merge with a sleeve, shoe proportions can change, and jewelry can shift position. Keep the source available and correct a local problem through the mask or a fresh edit. When an exact catalog detail cannot be retained reliably, use the real product artwork or a conventional composite.

Frequently asked questions​

Can I replace clothing using a product reference in Photoshop?​

Yes. Select the garment region, attach a clear product reference in the Astria panel, describe the replacement, and inspect the returned layer against both the source person and the product.

Does a clothing replacement guarantee the exact SKU?​

No. Review the pattern, color, neckline, seams, closures and proportions against the reference before using a result as a product image. Use a conventional composite for details that require exact reproduction.

How should a stylist present several outfit options?​

Keep the same source photograph and create named layers or groups for each combination. Show the source, proposed styling and associated product references together so the reviewer can judge the specific change.

entry.title: AI Packaging Mockups in Photoshop for Product Teams
entry.summary: Preview packaging patterns, logos, colors and product scenes in Photoshop. Use video examples and a practical workflow for design, brand and ecommerce teams.
entry.content:
A packaging designer needs to show a label wrapped around a jar. A brand manager wants to compare box colors and patterns. An ecommerce team needs a product scene that helps explain a launch concept.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin lets these teams use a package photograph and reference artwork to prepare visual mockups. Keep the approved artwork and package specification available throughout the review, then finish exact copy and print files in the normal design workflow.

Watch a plain box become a packaging concept​

The demonstration applies patterns and logos to jars, pouches and boxes, changes a lid and container appearance, and explores package colors and a product setting. The box sequence begins with a plain white package and develops a patterned blue concept.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Prepare the package and artwork as separate references​

A clear package photograph establishes the container's shape, closure and perspective. Approved artwork establishes the logo, pattern and text. Use each reference for its own role rather than asking a logo image to describe the physical package.

For a box, decide which graphics belong on the lid, front and side panels. For a jar or pouch, decide where the label starts and ends and which seams or transparent regions must remain visible. A brief with clear panel assignments is easier to review than a request to apply a general brand style everywhere.

Keep the actual dieline, dimensions and print artwork in the design document. The generated mockup helps stakeholders understand appearance; a print-ready layout still needs the original editable files and normal production review.

Build packaging alternatives one decision at a time​

Start with the plain package image and retain it on a base layer. Select the relevant panel, attach the artwork or pattern reference, and describe the assignment. Generate a candidate and inspect the edges where graphics meet folds, corners and the lid.

Make color and finish alternatives from the same base. If the question is whether a blue or neutral lid works better, keep the side pattern, camera and lighting consistent. Use a Photoshop color adjustment when that gives you the controlled comparison you need.

When changing transparent containers or visible contents, review how the material affects highlights, refraction and the label. A new fill must still sit inside a credible container rather than painting through the lid or erasing the glass boundary.

Finish logos and typography with original artwork​

Read every word rather than judging whether the package looks typographic. Compare the logo shape, spelling, spacing, small marks and placement with the approved file. Check whether a repeating pattern changes scale or direction between panels.

Use original logo and text layers for details that need exact reproduction. Transform or warp the artwork to the package perspective and refine the composite in Photoshop. This also makes a later legal-copy or product-name change editable without regenerating the complete package.

Prepare a lifestyle setting only after the package direction has been approved. Inspect contact shadows and the visible package against the source after placing it on a table or changing the background. Keep a clean product view available for the team that needs to judge the package itself.

entry.title: Portrait and Brand Photo Editing in Photoshop With AI
entry.summary: Adapt portrait backgrounds, wardrobe and styling with the Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin. A layered workflow for retouchers and in-house brand teams.
entry.content:
A brand designer needs a portrait that fits a new setting. A photographer wants to explore a wardrobe or hair variation. A communications team needs an approved image that works in a specific layout.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin lets an editor adapt an existing photograph, retain the source for comparison, and refine individual changes through Photoshop layers and masks. Begin with a photograph the subject or brand has approved.

Watch styling and setting changes​

The editing reel demonstrates pose changes, apparel colors, a reference garment, hair color, a beach setting, an office background, furniture and accessories. Each is a useful local or contextual editing task when the person and intended purpose remain clear.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Choose the change that serves the brief​

For an in-house brand photograph, a background change may be enough to make an image useful in a new layout. For a portrait styling exercise, wardrobe or hair can be the primary variable. Keep those decisions separate and preserve a version with the approved person and original appearance.

A small color shift is often best handled with a Photoshop adjustment layer. Use generation for a new environment, an item replacement or another change that requires reconstructed content. This keeps the retoucher's work focused and makes the approval conversation easier.

Attach the relevant reference when the brief calls for a specific garment, accessory or pose. The reference should answer the exact editing question. Avoid making an unrelated mood-board image responsible for the person's identity, wardrobe and background at once.

Change a background while preserving the portrait​

  1. Keep the approved photograph on a base layer and save the current selection or subject mask.
  2. Identify the background region and describe the intended setting and light direction.
  3. Specify the face, expression, clothing and pose to preserve.
  4. Generate an alternative and compare the returned layer with the base.
  5. Refine hair, shoulders, chair edges and any transparent or reflective detail.
  6. Balance the background and subject with Photoshop adjustments, then review at the final crop.

Look at the relationship between the person and the new setting. A seated subject needs credible chair and floor contact. Bright windows in the background should agree with light on the face. A convincing office should not introduce signage or brand marks that the communications team never approved.

Use a clear handoff for each role​

RoleApplicationApproval responsibility
Portrait photographerStyling alternatives and selected correctionsLikeness, expression and suitability for the subject
RetoucherLocal edits, background transitions and masksNatural detail and clean compositing
In-house brand designerAdapt a photograph to a campaign layoutBrand treatment, composition and artwork
Corporate communications teamReview a professional portrait presentationSubject approval and appropriate use
Social content designerExport approved crops and variantsReadability in the actual placement

Keep identity review close to the edit​

Compare eyes, mouth, hairline and distinctive features against the approved photograph. A change to gaze or expression can become a change to the person. When a face is turned away or obscured, another approved photograph can supply the visible features the edit needs.

Have the subject review material appearance changes before the image is used to represent them. Keep exact names, job titles and brand copy as editable text in the final layout. Save a layered master so the next request can change the background without regenerating the face.

Can I change a portrait background with Nano Banana in Photoshop?​

Yes. Use the source photograph as context, identify the background to replace, specify the subject features to preserve, and refine the returned layer at hair, shoulders and furniture edges.

entry.title: Real Estate Photo Editing in Photoshop With Nano Banana
entry.summary: Clean up property photos, explore staging and create twilight concepts in Photoshop. Practical Nano Banana workflows for photographers and property teams.
entry.content:
A property photograph needs clearer pool reflections, a tidier patio or a different lighting treatment. A staging designer wants to show how an outdoor seating area could feel with new cushions and planting.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin supports those editing and visualization tasks inside a layered document. Begin by deciding whether the image represents the property as it exists or illustrates a proposed presentation.

Watch pool and patio edits​

The property demonstration works on a pool courtyard and a house terrace. It refines lounge chairs and pool reflections, adds planting and decor, explores evening lighting, and changes the sky and cushions. These are useful examples of selecting a region and revising one part of a property image.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Choose between cleanup and proposed staging​

Removing a temporary distraction and adding furniture that is not present are different decisions. Keep the original photograph available and label staged or proposed versions so the team can choose the correct asset for a listing, a design presentation or an amenity concept.

For cleanup, select the distraction and describe the surrounding surface that should continue through the region. Review paving patterns, railings and furniture edges after the edit. Use conventional Photoshop tools for a small repair when the existing photograph already contains the needed detail.

For staging, provide the relevant furniture or planting references. Preserve the building envelope, openings and circulation space. Check whether the proposed seating still fits the visible area and whether people could reasonably move around it.

Create a twilight treatment from the same view​

Keep the camera and building form fixed while exploring the time of day. Allow the sky and illumination to change, then inspect windows, exterior fixtures and their reflected light. A darker sky with unchanged bright daylight on the facade often looks less convincing than a coherent treatment of the whole scene.

Refine local exposure and color with Photoshop adjustments after the edit. Avoid treating the generated lighting as a specification for the actual installed fixtures. For a future development, use the architecture Photoshop workflow with approved model exports.

Review reflections and repeated structures​

Pool water, glass doors and polished surfaces can reflect features that have changed elsewhere in the image. Inspect those reflections after adding a plant or changing the time of day. Check repeated chairs, paving joints, mullions and roof edges against the source; they are useful indicators of unintended reconstruction.

Review the final image with the person responsible for the property description. Confirm whether furniture, planting and lighting are existing or proposed. Export a clearly identified version and retain a layered master for corrections.

The most useful first exercise is one pool reflection repair or one patio staging option, rather than a complete reinterpretation of the property. Once the local edit is dependable, develop the wider atmosphere and presentation.

Can Nano Banana create a twilight property image?​

It can generate an evening interpretation from a property photograph. Keep the building and camera constraints explicit, then inspect facade light, windows, fixtures, sky and reflections together.

How should I present virtually staged property images?​

Keep the original photograph and identify furniture, planting or other additions as staged or proposed when presenting the image. Use the version that matches the purpose of the property communication.

What should I inspect after editing a pool or patio?​

Check reflections, water edges, furniture proportions, contact shadows, paving joints, doors and building boundaries against the original photograph.

entry.title: Nano Banana Photoshop Plugin V2: What Changed
entry.summary: Explore the rebuilt Nano Banana Photoshop plugin: drag-and-drop references, async generation, more consistent edits, agent automation, layer separation and video creation.
entry.content:
The Nano Banana Photoshop plugin V2 is a complete rewrite of Astria's Photoshop plugin. The new interface brings references, model settings and generation progress into one composer. You can keep working while an image generates, return the result as an editable layer, and use agent mode to automate Photoshop functions.

The update also improves selection placement and color handling, adds a workflow for separating a flat image into positioned layers, and lets you start video creation from the image already open in Photoshop.

What's new in the Photoshop plugin V2​

UpdateWhat it changes in daily work
Rebuilt interfaceReferences, prompt, model and supported output settings sit together in a compact composer.
Drag-and-drop referencesBring image files from Finder or Explorer into the panel on supported Photoshop hosts.
Async generationFollow progress or cancel in the panel while continuing other Photoshop work during generation.
More consistent placementMatching aspect ratios, uniform scaling, feathered masks and sRGB tagging reduce avoidable placement and color shifts.
Model choiceUse any model supported by the plugin's current catalog; the available controls adapt to it.
Agent modeAsk the connected agent to inspect and organize the document, or automate supported Photoshop functions.
Layer separationTurn a flat image into a base and positioned cutout Smart Objects inside a masked group.
Video creationSend a selection or visible image to Astria's browser workspace to plan and generate a video.

Here, V2 means the plugin version. It is separate from the name of any image model you choose inside the panel.

A composer built around the image you're editing​

A retoucher usually has three things to keep track of: the selected area, the requested change and the reference that defines it. The rebuilt panel keeps the reference thumbnails and instruction together, with model options close at hand. Resolution, quality and output count appear where the selected model supports them.

Add a product photograph from disk, capture the current Photoshop layer as a reference, or drag image files onto the panel. This makes an accessory swap or material study easier to set up: the reference remains visible while you write the change. For a step-by-step example, see using fashion references in Photoshop.

Drag-and-drop needs a compatible host: file drops into the panel require UXP 9.1 or later, such as Photoshop 2026. On an older supported Photoshop version, use Add image instead.

Keep working while the image generates​

V2 runs the generation request asynchronously. Photoshop captures the input, the panel follows the job, and you can continue working during the wait. Progress and cancellation live inside the panel.

For a production retoucher, that can mean preparing another document while a replacement background generates. An art director can work on a presentation layout while an image variation is in progress. There is less pressure to turn each generation into a separate pause in the working day.

Source capture and result placement still briefly need Photoshop access. Keep the source document's dimensions and placement unchanged until the result returns; work in another document when you need to change those. Agent tools also wait until the active panel generation has finished.

Less drift when results return to the document​

A good generated edit can still create extra work if it comes back stretched, misaligned or with an unexpected color shift. The rewritten editing pipeline addresses those problems:

  • Aspect ratio and scaling: requests follow the selected region's proportions, and placement uses uniform scaling rather than stretching the result.
  • Selection blending: a softly feathered mask helps the generated area meet the original image.
  • Color handling: sRGB tagging reduces mismatches when generated images enter documents using another color profile.
  • Editable delivery: results return as Smart Objects, so masks and ordinary Photoshop adjustments remain available.

These changes reduce avoidable drift in the editing workflow. A model can still reinterpret a face, garment, product detail or architectural feature. Compare the result with the original before approving it, especially when exact product shape or building geometry matters.

For architecture teams, this is useful when reviewing facade materials, interior finishes or lighting alternatives. Keep the approved geometry as the base and treat generated variations as design studies. The architecture workflow guide covers those review tasks in more detail.

Choose the model for the task​

You can switch between models supported by the plugin without changing the way you prepare a Photoshop selection. The panel reads the available catalog and shows the controls appropriate to the chosen model.

That gives a studio room to try a different model when an edit needs another approach. A tool such as layer separation has a different input workflow from a reference-based image edit, so its controls change too. Check the current picker for availability rather than building a process around a fixed list of model names.

Agent mode for Photoshop automation​

Open agent mode from the plugin to give the agent a connection to the current Photoshop document. It can inspect document and layer information, organize layers and run supported Photoshop functions. Repetitive work can be expressed as a brief instead of a long sequence of clicks.

Useful starting requests include:

Inspect the open document and list its layers before making any changes.

Group the selected layers into a group called “Client review” and give the layers clear, descriptive names.

For more involved tasks, the agent can use scripts for loops, conditional edits and calculated layouts. Describe the intended result and the layers it should affect. Check the resulting document before handing it to another person.

The Photoshop connection comes from opening the agent inside the plugin. A regular Astria browser chat does not have that document connection. Finish an active panel generation before asking the agent to run Photoshop tools.

Separate a flat image into editable layers​

Layer separation gives you a way to work with individual parts of an image that arrived as a single flattened file. Select the area to separate—use Select All for the whole image—then choose the layer separation model. You can leave the instruction empty or describe the elements you want separated.

The result arrives as positioned cutout Smart Objects above a base, arranged in stacking order inside one masked group. The import is grouped into one undo step. This creates a useful starting point for compositing and local adjustments; inspect edges and overlaps before final delivery.

The release announcement illustrates another example below: a fashion photograph separated into the subject, handbag, stools and scene elements. Its colored outlines explain the breakdown; they are annotations, not the Photoshop masks. The ten-layer result belongs to this example, rather than a fixed layer count for every image.

Start a video from your Photoshop image​

The Create video camera button captures the selected area, or the whole visible image when there is no selection. Your prompt can travel with it as a starting brief.

The workflow then continues in Astria's browser workspace, where the storyboard agent helps plan the shots and generate the video. This gives a motion designer or campaign team a path from an approved still to a moving concept. The handoff opens that video workflow; it does not place a generated clip into Photoshop's timeline.

Where V2 fits across a creative team​

RolePractical useWhat to review
RetoucherReference-based accessory changes, cleanup and background edits while preparing other filesMask edges, skin detail and local color matching
Ecommerce or merchandising leadExplore product styling and campaign variations with supplied referencesShape, color, logos and SKU details against the real product
Architect or interior designerCompare materials, shades and atmosphere on an existing concept viewGeometry, perspective and consistency with the design brief
Creative director or studio leadOrganize document layers with the agent and review alternate treatmentsClear version names and an editable handoff
Motion designer or social creativeSend an approved still into storyboard and video creationSubject continuity, framing and the intended movement

For packaging teams, the packaging mockup workflow shows how to evaluate visual concepts while retaining a controlled master design.

Update the plugin and try one real task​

Download the latest maintained CCX build from the Nano Banana Photoshop plugin page. The plugin supports Photoshop 2025, version 26 and later, on macOS and Windows; use Photoshop 2026 or another compatible host for file drag-and-drop.

Open a working copy of an image, make a selection, add a reference if the chosen model supports it, and describe one specific change. Review the returned Smart Object beside the original. Then try layer separation or open the agent for a document organization task.

See Astria pricing for current terms. The Photoshop plugin guide covers the broader editing workflow.

Watch the V2 demonstration​

The demo shows reference edits and layer separation. Its interface reflects the recorded build; agent and video workflows described above are available in the updated plugin. The public V2 release announcement covers the rebuilt panel and selection pipeline.

Frequently asked questions​

Can I keep working in Photoshop while an image generates?​

Yes. The network generation runs asynchronously, so you can keep working while the panel shows progress. Capturing the source and placing the result briefly require Photoshop access. Keep the source document geometry unchanged until the result returns.

Which Photoshop versions support the plugin and drag-and-drop?​

The maintained plugin supports Photoshop 2025, version 26 and later, on macOS and Windows. Dropping files into the panel needs a host with UXP 9.1 or later, such as Photoshop 2026. Use Add image on older supported hosts.

Does V2 mean the Nano Banana 2 image model?​

No. V2 names the rebuilt Astria Photoshop plugin. The plugin can use models available in its model picker, with controls adapting to the selected model.

Can the Photoshop AI agent organize layers?​

Yes. Open agent mode from the plugin to inspect the document and automate supported Photoshop functions, including naming layers and creating groups. Photoshop tools require the plugin connection, and cannot run while a panel generation is active.

Where does video creation happen?​

Create video captures the selection, or the visible image if there is no selection, and opens an Astria browser workspace for storyboard planning and video generation. The handoff does not insert a generated video into the Photoshop timeline.

entry.title: Wedding Photo Retouching in Photoshop With Nano Banana
entry.summary: Remove distractions and refine bridal photographs in Photoshop with Nano Banana. A workflow for wedding photographers, retouchers and album designers.
entry.content:
A guest raises a phone into the frame. A hand covers part of the bride's hair. The best expression arrives in a photograph with a distracting background. These are specific editing problems inside an otherwise useful wedding photograph.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin lets a photographer select the affected region, describe a correction, and refine the result on a separate layer. Keep the couple's identity, the dress and the character of the event central to every decision.

Watch distraction removal and bridal refinements​

The demonstration includes ground cleanup, warm lighting, dress-train changes, hand and phone removal, hair refinement, makeup, and creative pose or setting changes. Those edits serve different purposes: cleaning an obstruction preserves the intended photograph, while changing the dress or setting creates a new interpretation for the client's review.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Start with one distraction​

Keep an untouched copy of the photograph. Select the unwanted phone, hand or background object with enough surrounding context to reconstruct what it covers. Avoid including the face or dress unnecessarily when they are already satisfactory.

The editing brief should identify the obstruction and what must remain: the person's facial features, pose, dress construction, crop and existing light direction. Generate a correction, toggle it against the source, and inspect the region at full size before continuing. Hair, fingers, jewelry and lace deserve particular attention because their fine shapes can become convincing but incorrect substitutes.

If the covered area contains a meaningful detail, another photograph from the same sequence can provide reference evidence. A dress button, ring or embroidered panel is easier to restore from the real event than to reconstruct from a generic description.

Keep retouching and creative restyling separate​

For a small exposure or skin-color adjustment, use a normal Photoshop adjustment layer. Use generation when removing an obstruction or changing a scene requires content that the photograph does not already contain.

Make a warm evening treatment in a separate group from the cleanup. Compare the original light and the new atmosphere at the same crop. A golden treatment should still retain natural skin color and distinguish the dress from the background.

The video also explores a longer dress train, a veil and changes to pose or background. Present those as creative alternatives. A client who wants an accurate record of the day should be able to choose the corrected original without also accepting an invented garment or setting.

Organize the handoff inside the studio​

RoleWhat to use the plugin forWhat to approve
Wedding photographerRecover a useful frame with a local distractionIdentity, expression and fidelity to the event
Bridal retoucherReconstruct small obscured areas and refine masksHair, hands, jewelry, lace and edit boundaries
Studio art directorReview a cinematic or warm treatmentNatural skin, dress separation and consistency
Album designerSelect images that work together on the pageCrop, color continuity and the final print appearance
Client service teamExplain optional creative changesThe client's selection of the original or altered version

Review at delivery size​

Judge the finished image both at full size and in the actual album layout. A clean edge on screen can become a distracting halo around hair in print. Look at the transition into the unedited photograph, contact shadows, and any detail that was hidden by the removed object.

Save a layered master and export the approved version. Naming groups by the decision, such as cleanup or evening treatment, makes later client feedback actionable. Keep the original available when a revision should undo only the creative treatment.

For editorial garment imagery, see wedding dress photography prompts. For the panel setup, read the Nano Banana Photoshop guide.

Get the Astria Photoshop plugin for selection-based corrections in your document. See Astria pricing for current terms.

Frequently asked questions​

Can Nano Banana remove a phone from a wedding photograph?​

Select the phone and the area it obscures, describe its removal, and review the reconstructed region on the returned Photoshop layer. Supply another event photograph as a reference when a hidden dress, hand or jewelry detail matters.

Should I use AI to change a bride's pose or dress?​

Treat pose, wardrobe and setting changes as creative alternatives and let the client choose them separately from corrections to the original photograph.

What should I inspect after removing an obstructing hand?​

Check the reconstructed hair, skin, garment edges and jewelry against the source and any supporting photograph. Refine the layer mask and review the result at the intended print or album size.

entry.title: Nano Banana Architecture in Photoshop for Design Teams
entry.summary: Turn sketches and exported model views into architectural concepts in Photoshop. Compare materials, interiors, lighting and development scenarios.
entry.content:
An architect needs to explain a facade option. An interior designer needs to compare finishes in the same room. A development manager needs an image that makes a proposed project understandable to stakeholders. Each needs a visual of a specific change, with the existing design still legible.

The Astria Nano Banana Photoshop plugin lets you start with a sketch, a photograph or an exported model view, describe the change, and review the result in a layered Photoshop document. Use it to explore materials, atmosphere and presentation while keeping the underlying design in your modeling application.

Watch a sketch become a realistic concept​

The architecture demonstration starts with a line drawing of a modern house and pool. It creates a daylight interpretation, then explores night lighting, blue pool illumination, outdoor dining and a different viewpoint. The source is already an image in Photoshop.

Select an image to enlarge it. Frames are cropped from the original video.

Watch the original Astria demonstration. The recording shows an earlier plugin interface; use the current panel for the selection, reference-image and returned-layer workflow. Illustrations are stills from that recording.

Match the image to the project decision​

Team roleDecision to supportPhotoshop workflow
Building architectExplain the character of an early designMaterialize a sketch or a clay-render export using the intended palette
Interior designerCompare flooring, cabinetry and upholsterySelect one surface or furnishing group and attach finish references
Visualization artistImprove the realism of a model exportWork on material appearance, reflections, planting and atmosphere
Lighting designerDiscuss day, evening and pool lightingKeep the source view fixed and compare separate lighting interpretations
Development managerCommunicate alternative schemes or project phasesExport each designed option first, then apply a consistent visual treatment
Design director or project leadReview options with the clientKeep alternatives in named layers and show the same crop for each
Developer marketing teamExplain the planned experience of an amenityPrepare clearly labeled concept images from approved project views

Explore lighting and viewpoints separately​

A viewpoint change reveals surfaces the original drawing never supplied. For a client presentation that must match the design, set the camera in Blender, SketchUp or CAD and export that view first. This also lets a project team compare several angles against one authoritative model.

For surface shades, begin with Photoshop adjustment layers when the geometry and texture already work. Use generation when a change needs a new material appearance or reconstructed reflections. Keep lighting variations separate from material comparisons so the brighter image does not become the accidental favorite.

Start with the decision, then choose the size of the edit​

A useful architecture image answers a question. Decide what can change and what must remain fixed before generating.

LevelTypical questionStarting imagePhotoshop approach
City or districtHow would this approved development sit in its surroundings?Oblique view exported from a site modelSelect the development area; retain surrounding context
Neighborhood or campusWhat character should the public spaces have?Massing view with paths and courtyards establishedEdit ground treatments, planting, and street furniture
Road or streetHow would a proposed street redesign look at eye level?Street photograph with a designed intervention composited into itSelect the proposal footprint; keep buildings and junctions fixed
BuildingHow could this clay model read as a finished building?Neutral render from the architect's modelApply a material palette across the full view
RenovationWhat can change while keeping the existing shell?Site photograph or proposed-model renderEdit finishes or a separately modeled addition
InteriorWhich finish and furniture combination suits this room?Room photograph or renderChange one surface or furnishing group at a time
DetailWould a different screen, handle, or joint treatment work visually?Close view of the relevant assemblyMake a small selection and inspect at full size

These are presentation workflows. A realistic image does not establish dimensions, buildability, or performance. Keep the surveyed information, geometry, and technical decisions in the project model and drawings.

Set up the Photoshop document​

Export a clear view from your modeling or rendering application, or open a project photograph you have permission to use. For a clay render, make window recesses, slab edges, entrances, and ground levels legible. A featureless white block gives the model little evidence about the intended facade.

Keep an untouched base layer. Save selections for recurring edit areas, and put each alternative in a named group: Facade — brick, Facade — limestone, or Kitchen — oak fronts. Hide earlier alternatives before generating the next one so they do not become part of its input.

Open the Astria panel through Photoshop's Plugins menu. The current plugin requires Photoshop 2025, version 26 or later, on macOS or Windows. Its documented workflow accepts selections and reference images and returns an edit as a new layer. See the plugin and installation page.

In version 2, references can come from an image file or the current Photoshop layer. The panel exposes model-dependent controls and handles contextual capture and blending around the selection. Those conveniences still need a visual check at building edges and material boundaries. Astria's version 2 release notes describe the changes.

For each edit:

  1. Select the intended area. Use a polygonal selection or a path for planar surfaces. Exclude windows, reveals, fixtures, and other elements that must stay.
  2. Attach relevant references. Use a material sample for a material edit, a furniture photograph for a furniture edit, or a palette board for a full-view treatment. Name each reference's role in the prompt.
  3. Choose the model and output settings. Start comparisons at the same supported resolution, with the same output count. Choose a supported resolution suited to the final presentation and inspect the returned pixel dimensions.
  4. Describe the change and the constraints. State what to alter, which reference governs it, and what to preserve.
  5. Review the returned layer. Toggle it against the base; inspect the mask, perspective, repeated elements, and neighboring pixels. Refine the mask in Photoshop before showing the option to a client.

For material alternatives, keep camera and lighting consistent. For intentional lighting changes, check whether your panel's Generate menu offers Generate with the prompt only: this omits the added preservation instruction in builds that expose it. Put the geometry and camera constraints in your own prompt, while explicitly allowing the lighting change.

1. Building architects: turn a clay render into a realistic concept​

Decision: can the client understand the architectural character before the full material setup is complete?

Start with a courtyard building rendered in neutral gray. Include the actual openings, balcony edges, paving levels, and roofline. Add a reference board containing the intended limestone, bronze metalwork, and paving. Use the whole view as the selection for this first treatment.

Turn the supplied clay render into a realistic architectural concept image.
Use the clay render as the authority for geometry and camera position.
Use the attached material board only for material appearance: pale limestone
on the opaque facade, bronze metal on the existing frames, and warm gray
paving on the existing courtyard surface. Keep the building outline,
number and position of openings, floor count, balcony depths, roofline,
ground levels, crop, and perspective unchanged. Retain the direction of
the source shadows. Introduce realistic surface texture and reflections
without adding architectural elements.

Try Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro on the same input. Compare the result by counting windows and checking slab edges before judging atmosphere. Add Seedream or another reference-capable model only with the same source, references, prompt, and framing.

The useful before/after shows the clay view beside the materialized view, with matching crops. A more dramatic image that adds a floor or moves the entrance is a failed interpretation of this brief.

“Clay to real” here means visual interpretation. For sun, wind, daylight, or microclimate evaluation, use tools that calculate those quantities from the project data; Autodesk's Forma analysis documentation illustrates that separate workflow.

2. Facade designers: compare materials without redesigning the building​

Decision: should the same facade use brick, stone, or metal?

Select the opaque cladding on one elevation. Subtract glazing, mullions, balcony rails, soffits, and neighboring buildings. Save that selection. Generate each option from the original view, with its corresponding material reference.

Replace only the selected opaque facade cladding with the terracotta brick
shown in the material reference. Follow its warm red-brown color variation
and matte surface. Use horizontal running-bond courses with a consistent
module across the elevation. Preserve the existing facade plane, all
window openings, frames, sills, balcony rails, roofline, perspective,
lighting, and everything outside the cladding selection.

For the limestone option, change the material instruction and reference while keeping the remaining brief fixed. Distinguish this design-option comparison from a model comparison, where even the requested material stays identical.

Look closely at corners and window returns: does the treatment wrap convincingly, or does the model paint a flat texture across the openings? Exact bond dimensions, panel sizes, and fixing details belong in the facade design. If a joint must land precisely, draw it or model it and use that as the next reference.

3. Home renovation architects: show a finish refresh and an extension separately​

Decision: what can the homeowner achieve by changing finishes, and what requires a physical alteration?

For a finish refresh, use the existing photograph. Select cabinet fronts and end panels, keeping the countertop, appliance openings, sink, and wall geometry outside the selection.

Change only the selected kitchen cabinet fronts and exposed end panels
to the natural oak finish in the supplied sample. Keep grain direction
vertical on the doors. Preserve every door and drawer division, handle
position, appliance opening, countertop, sink, backsplash, room boundary,
camera position, and existing light direction. Keep the countertop edge
and cabinet shadow gaps clearly defined.

For an extension, first model the proposed volume and openings, then export the same camera view. Use that view to explore cladding and atmosphere. Asking the image model to invent an extension from a photograph leaves roof junctions, heights, and internal relationships unresolved.

Present the existing photograph, finish-only proposal, and modeled-extension visualization as separate options with explicit labels. That helps the client understand the scope of each decision.

4. Interior designers: change a floor, then furniture, then the mood​

Decision: which material palette works in the actual room?

Begin with one surface. Select the visible floor while excluding furniture, skirting, and door thresholds. Attach a flooring reference that shows several boards or tiles, rather than an ambiguous close-up.

Replace the selected floor finish with the pale oak flooring in the
reference image. Run the boards toward the far window, following the
room's perspective. Preserve the room dimensions, walls, skirting,
door thresholds, furniture positions, and camera. Retain contact shadows
under the furniture and the original direction of daylight. Do not
change any wall or furniture finishes.

Next, make a separate furniture edit with a product reference. Include the object's footprint and contact shadow in the selection. Inspect legs, seams, proportions, and occlusion; reference-based generation does not guarantee an exact catalog match. Composite the actual product cutout when exact product identity is required.

A convincing comparison uses the same room and exposure for both palettes. Otherwise, clients may prefer the brighter picture rather than the better material combination.

5. Detail designers: test a screen, balustrade, or hardware change​

Decision: how does a local detail affect the composition?

For an entrance screen, start from a view where its frame and opening are already designed. Select the infill and supply a photograph or drawing of the proposed screen pattern.

Replace only the selected entrance-screen infill with the vertical bronze
fins shown in the reference. Fit the fins inside the existing frame and
follow the perspective of that frame. Preserve the frame outline,
adjacent door, glazing, wall finish, ground, camera, and light direction.
Do not extend fins across the doorway or alter the entrance width.

Compare a mask-aware model such as GPT Image 2 with a reference-capable Gemini model. The question is whether the edit stays local and respects the frame. If exact fin count or spacing matters, place a drawn pattern first and ask for a material treatment of that pattern.

For a paint color, handle swap, or minor alignment correction, a conventional adjustment layer or transformed product cutout may be sufficient. Reserve generation for changes that need a new material appearance, reflected environment, or contextual reconstruction.

6. Neighborhood and campus planners: make a massing study legible​

Decision: what would the spaces between the buildings feel like?

Use an oblique site-model view with the building volumes, streets, paths, and courtyards already established. Select one public-space area and provide a landscape palette. Work on one block or courtyard before trying to reinterpret an entire district.

Develop the selected courtyard into a realistic public-space concept
using the supplied paving and planting references. Keep all building
footprints, heights, entrances, street edges, paths, and camera position
as shown in the source model. Add planting only inside the existing
planting beds and benches only within the designated seating areas.
Keep the central walking route open. Preserve the surrounding blocks.

Prepare more than one view from the same underlying model if the proposal needs both an aerial explanation and a pedestrian experience. Treat each generated image as a separate interpretation and check materials and features across views.

For development phasing, export each phase from the model first, then apply a consistent visual treatment. Keep phase colors, boundaries, labels, and legends on ordinary Photoshop layers so the presentation remains unambiguous.

7. City planners and road designers: visualize an approved street proposal​

Decision: how can a proposed street change be explained to residents or stakeholders?

Start with a licensed street photograph and a perspective overlay of the designed curb, path, and planting geometry. Select the intervention footprint. The overlay supplies the spatial arrangement; the image model supplies a possible material and landscape appearance.

Render the proposed street intervention shown in the supplied composite.
Use the overlaid curb and cycle-track geometry as the authority for the
layout. Replace the marked parking strip with the shown cycle track and
planting islands. Keep the existing building facades, junction positions,
crossing locations, horizon, camera, and all unmarked street areas
unchanged. Use the attached paving and planting references. Do not add
traffic lanes, move intersections, or invent signs and road markings.

Check continuity through the image: does the cycle track disappear behind a tree, jump across a crossing, or narrow unexpectedly? Keep required markings and labels as deliberate overlays when generation cannot reproduce them reliably.

NACTO's neighborhood-street guidance is useful background for the design conversation. A Photoshop visualization can communicate a proposal; the road layout still needs its normal design and engineering review.

At city scale, use district views to explain an established massing strategy. Retain the authoritative land-use map, transport network, and annotations separately rather than asking the model to redraw them.

8. Landscape architects: compare planting character and seasonal appearance​

Decision: should a courtyard feel open and meadow-like, or more structured and shaded?

Start from the same landscape model or photograph. Select the established planting beds, keeping paths, levels, drainage features, and entrances fixed. Supply references for the intended planting character.

Change vegetation only within the selected planting beds to the meadow
character shown in the reference photographs: fine grasses and low
flowering perennials. Keep path edges, paving, retaining walls, ground
levels, existing tree positions, and building entrances unchanged.
Keep planting clear of the visible walking routes. Preserve the camera
and the original lighting.

Make a second seasonal interpretation from the same source, with a season-specific reference. Label it as an illustrative seasonal view. Check species appearance and planting scale against the actual planting schedule; the picture does not establish growth, survival, water use, or cooling performance.

9. Conservation and adaptive-reuse teams: explore reversible interventions​

Decision: how would a new use read inside an existing structure?

Use a measured-model view or a project photograph with protected fabric clearly identified. Select only the proposed furniture, freestanding partitions, or new finish area. Attach references for the intervention.

Within the selected area, visualize the freestanding reception desk shown
in the design reference. Preserve the existing masonry, columns, beams,
window openings, floor levels, and all visible historic surface detail.
Keep the desk separate from the existing columns and retain the camera
and light direction. Do not restore, clean, replace, or invent details
on the existing building fabric.

Show the original next to the proposal and identify the added elements. For restoration studies, use archival or measured evidence for missing features; stylistic plausibility is insufficient evidence of what was originally there.

10. Hospitality, workplace, and retail designers: compare fit-out concepts​

Decision: how would a different interior identity work within the same shell?

A hotel lobby, office reception, or cafe can share the same method: retain the approved layout and change a defined palette or furnishing group. Use a reference board with clearly labeled materials and objects.

Restyle only the selected cafe banquette and wall panels using the
reference board: muted olive upholstery on the existing seats and
natural walnut veneer on the existing panels. Preserve the seating
layout, table count and positions, aisle boundaries, windows, ceiling,
camera, and light direction. Keep upholstery and veneer assigned to
their specified surfaces. Do not introduce signs or lettering.

Place logos, wayfinding, and exact text as editable Photoshop artwork after the edit. For lighting mood options, work from a separate copy of the approved view and explicitly allow lighting to change. Evaluate illumination levels with the lighting-design workflow, rather than reading them from the generated image.

Choose a model for the architectural edit​

Nano Banana is Google's name for a family of image models, not one fixed model. Google's image-generation documentation distinguishes Nano Banana 2 from Nano Banana Pro and describes image-guided editing and resolution options.

The table below is a testing plan, not an architecture benchmark or a ranking. Confirm the current models and controls in your installed panel.

Model to testArchitecture taskWhat to compare
Nano Banana 2Clay-to-real and initial material optionsOpenings, silhouette, perspective, and material assignment
Nano Banana ProThe same clay view or a detailed multi-reference briefWhether constraints and reference roles survive the edit
GPT Image 2A selected cabinet, screen, or facade detailLocality of the edit, edge quality, and surrounding pixels
Seedream 5 / 5 ProThe same facade or interior material briefTexture scale, repeated patterns, and unintended redesign
Flux 2 ProThe same photographic material or landscape editSurface appearance, shadows, and preservation of the source

Astria lists these model families on its Photoshop plugin page. Resolution and reference support vary by model and integration; verify the selected model's controls instead of assuming every model supports the same settings.

Photoshop's native Generative Fill also supports partner models and reference images, as Adobe documents. Evaluate Astria around its actual panel workflow and available models, rather than the outdated claim that Photoshop only offers Adobe models.

Compare models on the same architectural problem​

Choose one base image and one edit. Keep the reference files and their order, prompt, selection, source-layer visibility, aspect ratio, resolution, and output count fixed across compatible models. Record any model-specific control or input-path difference.

For local editing, distinguish what the model returned from what the Photoshop mask reveals. A good final composite can conceal changes elsewhere in the returned image. Review both before claiming that a model preserved the geometry.

Use four checks:

  • Geometry: building outline, openings, slab edges, perspective, and repeated elements.
  • Reference fidelity: material color, pattern, grain direction, object shape, and scale cues.
  • Edit boundaries: unintended changes, halos, broken shadows, and seams.
  • Presentation quality: credibility and clarity at the size the client will actually see.

Record manual cleanup separately. A model that needs substantial repair may still be useful, but the repaired composite should not be presented as the untouched output.

Finish with a decision-ready presentation​

Show the source and alternatives at the same crop and size. Label the material or design change, identify concept imagery, and keep exact dimensions, notes, and product references editable. Save the layered PSD so the next client comment becomes a specific revision.

The most useful starting exercise is a single material swap on a familiar project. Once that workflow is dependable, extend it to a clay render, an interior palette, or a public-space proposal.

Get the Astria Photoshop plugin, and consult Astria pricing for current terms.

Frequently asked questions​

Can Nano Banana turn a SketchUp or Blender render into a realistic image?​

Export an image from SketchUp, Blender or your CAD application, open it in Photoshop, and use that view as the reference for an image edit. The plugin edits pixels; it does not import or update the native project model.

Can I change materials and lighting without changing the design?​

Select the relevant surfaces, supply material references, and specify the camera and geometry to preserve. Review openings, edges and repeated elements against the source. For an accurate new viewpoint, export that camera from the project model first.

Is an AI architectural image a project simulation?​

It is a concept visualization for communicating appearance and comparing design options. Dimensions, construction, daylight, energy and engineering performance require the project model and the relevant analysis tools.

entry.title: 1.8: How to Choose Product Reference Photos for AI Fashion Images
entry.summary: Choose useful product reference photos for Astria: prepare clear garment images, add distinctive back details, use a shoe angle and explain missing fit information.
entry.content:
Astria Workshops · Series 1: Your first AI lookbook · Lesson 8

Choose reference photos that explain your product’s shape, color and details. More references are not always better: extra images that add no useful information can make the direction less clear.

Follow workshop 1.8: Troubleshooting AI. You’ll prepare the product, identify missing views, choose a shoe reference, match inputs to the crop and use a short prompt to clarify fit.

Before you begin​

Gather the original photos of the products you want to show. Open the look you’re working on in Astria Generate, and keep your shot list nearby. It tells you which details and products must appear in each image.

Step 1: Make the product easy to see​

For a simple T-shirt, a clear phone photo may be enough. For more detailed garments, consider a DSLR camera with even flash lighting. Keep the white balance consistent so the colors look accurate.

Iron out unwanted creases before shooting: they may appear in the generated image too. Keep the garment’s real seams and details visible.

Step 2: Add back views when they provide missing information​

Look for details the front photo does not explain. Add a back photo when the garment has a back logo, a print or a different color. For a T-shirt with a plain back, a front photo may be enough.

If a generated back view repeats a print that belongs only on the front, state that the back is plain in the prompt. Check the next result against the real garment.

Step 3: Choose a useful shoe angle​

When shoes support the outfit, use one clear photo from the front at about 45 degrees. It shows the toe and side together. Several similar views may not add useful information.

When shoes are the main product, extra references may help show their details. Choose them for what each one adds.

Step 4: Match the references to the framing​

Include a shoe reference in a full-length image that shows the shoes. If the shot crops them out, remove that reference. Keep the inputs focused on what you want in the image.

Step 5: Use the prompt for information the photos do not explain​

Some information is easier to express in words. Add what the photos leave unclear and keep the instruction focused. You do not need a long description copied from another chat.

For example, a flat product photo of balloon jeans may not explain how roomy they should look on the body. Add “balloon fitting” to describe the intended fit.

Generate, compare the fit with the real garment and adjust the wording if it still needs work. The workshop’s balloon-jeans example is a separate FRAME product; it is not the burgundy Bobo Choses trousers used earlier in the series.

Check your result​

Check that every reference contributes useful information. Your photos should explain the product’s visible details, and the prompt should clarify what those photos cannot show. Compare the output with the real garment’s shape, color and details before keeping it.

entry.title: 1.7: How to Choose Poses and Framing for AI Product Photos
entry.summary: Choose poses and framing for AI product photos in Astria. Study garment galleries, build a shot list, use Lookbook Pose and review consistent views.

Astria Workshops · Series 1: Your first AI lookbook · Lesson 7

Choose poses and framing that help a shopper understand the garment. You already have a look you’re happy with; now you’ll plan the views that show its fit, shape and details.

Before you begin​
